app.name: CrispDeck
app.subtitle: Mastodon · Bluesky · Threads
app.description:
One app for Mastodon, Bluesky and Threads — read them together, post to all three at once, and watch them in a deck of live columns.

THREE NETWORKS, ONE PLACE
Mastodon and Bluesky are built on entirely different protocols, and Threads on neither. CrispDeck speaks all three and puts them in one timeline, one search and one composer. Connect as many accounts as you like, on any instance.

POST ONCE, EVERYWHERE
Write a message and send it to every network in one go. Anything too long for Bluesky's 300 characters is split into a properly numbered thread there, posted whole on Mastodon, and crossposted to Threads. Mentions are resolved to the right handle on each network before anything is sent. Add images or video with alt text — required, warned about, or optional, your choice — polls, content warnings, reply controls and self-labels.

A DECK THAT WATCHES FOR YOU
Build a wall of columns from twenty types: home timelines, mentions, hashtags, lists, custom feeds, searches, RSS, messages, trending and more. Colour them, pin them, resize them, save whole layouts as workspaces.

Keyword-monitor columns stream live from the Bluesky Jetstream firehose and the Mastodon streaming API, filtered by your own words and regular expressions, so a term you care about surfaces the moment somebody uses it.

BUILD A FEED AND PUBLISH IT
The feed builder lets you assemble a custom Bluesky algorithm from filter rules, preview exactly what it catches, and publish it to the network as a real feed generator that anyone on Bluesky can subscribe to.

KNOW YOUR OWN ACCOUNTS
Identity mapping links the same person's accounts across networks. Cross-platform analytics compare your reach side by side — best posting times, day-of-week and hourly patterns, engagement milestones — and a local archive keeps your posts and likes searchable offline, exportable as JSON, CSV or Markdown.

EVERYTHING ELSE
Threads with full reply chains and "read as article", profiles, bookmarks synced with Bluesky's own, Mastodon lists and announcements, starter packs, labellers and moderation controls, muted words, direct messages, scheduled posts and drafts that survive a crash, translation through five providers including your own instance, a content calendar, a media gallery and reading lists.

PRIVATE BY DEFAULT
No accounts with us, no advertising, no analytics, no tracking. Everything is stored on your device, and credentials are encrypted with AES-256-GCM. CrispDeck is open source under the AGPL-3.0.

Built with Tauri 2, SvelteKit and Rust.
app.promotionalText: Mastodon, Bluesky and Threads in one deck: crosspost with automatic thread splitting, watch keywords live off the firehose, and publish your own Bluesky feed.

review.notes:
CrispDeck is a client for three social networks at once: Mastodon (ActivityPub), Bluesky (AT Protocol) and Threads (Meta Graph API).

SIGNING IN
No demo account is provided, because CrispDeck has no accounts of its own — it signs in to an account you already hold on one of those networks. If you do not have one, a free account at mastodon.social takes about a minute and exercises the whole app.

Settings > Accounts > Add Mastodon > enter the instance (for example mastodon.social) > authorise in the browser. The feed, deck and compose screens populate once an account is connected; before that the app is deliberately empty.

WHAT IT DOES
Multi-column deck of timelines, mentions, searches, hashtags and lists; composing and crossposting one message to several networks at once, with long posts split into threads automatically.

PRIVACY
Credentials are stored on the device and never reach our servers. The only first-party network calls are an optional Threads OAuth proxy and an optional web-push relay; everything else goes directly to the network the user chose.
review._demoAccountComment: REQUIRED before submitting. A social client shows nothing behind the sign-in wall, and 1.2.6 was reviewed with no way in at all. Create one Mastodon and one Bluesky account for review, put the Mastodon address and password here, and put the Bluesky handle and app password in the notes below. listing.py refuses to run while these are empty.
review._demoComment: false, and the notes say why. This was true with demoAccountName and demoAccountPassword both empty, and notes telling the reviewer to use DEMO_BSKY_HANDLE / DEMO_BSKY_APP_PASSWORD — placeholders that were never filled in. Submitting that promises a demo account and then supplies credentials that do not exist, which is a rejection. CrispDeck has no accounts of its own: it signs in to the reviewer's existing account on Mastodon, Bluesky or Threads. Saying so plainly is the honest answer and is what Beta App Review approved for 1.2.8.

beta.description: CrispDeck is a multi-platform client for Mastodon, Bluesky, and Threads. Crosspost, translate, schedule, and browse with a multi-column deck layout.
beta.whatToTest:
1.2.9 is 129 commits past the 1.2.8 build, and most of it is correctness work rather than features.

Worth exercising:
- Connecting accounts. Mastodon sign-in was rewritten: the callback now refuses an authorisation that did not come from the sign-in you started.
- Adding an account you already have connected. It used to overwrite the connected account's stored credentials; it now refuses with a sentence.
- Going offline mid-session. The feed, notifications and trending should each say they are showing cached data, and clear that themselves when the connection returns.
- Block vs mute on Bluesky. Block used to perform a mute.
- The deck: twenty column types, most of which have never been used against real data.

Credentials on iOS live in the app's own encrypted store rather than the iOS keychain. Please report anything that loses an account.
beta._extraComment: Appended to whatToTest for that platform only. macOS and iOS do not store credentials the same way and the macOS path is the one nobody has run on real hardware, so its testers are told.
beta.whatToTestExtra_macos:
MACOS-SPECIFIC, PLEASE READ
The desktop build stores account credentials in the macOS Keychain. That code is covered by tests against real keychains on CI, but nobody has yet driven it from the settings screen on an actual Mac — this build is the first time that path meets real hardware.

So the thing most worth your attention is anything to do with accounts:
- Connect an account, quit CrispDeck completely, reopen it. Is the account still there and still working?
- Settings > Credentials lets you choose which keychain is used (login, or one you made yourself with `security create-keychain`). Try switching it, then connect another account.
- If a keychain prompt appears, what does it say, and does saying no leave the app in a sensible state?

If an account disappears or stops working after a restart, that is the bug we most want to hear about, and the log viewer (Settings > Debug log) has a download button.
beta.whatToTestExtra_ios: iOS keeps credentials in the app's own encrypted store rather than the iOS keychain, so an account that vanishes after a restart is worth reporting.

ageRating._comment: The human decision, recorded so it is reviewable in git rather than typed into a browser. appstore.md records: all NONE/false except unrestrictedWebAccess and userGeneratedContent. Both are true here — CrispDeck renders posts from arbitrary fediverse users and opens links to arbitrary sites. DEVIATION: messagingAndChat is also true, which appstore.md does not list. The app has direct messages (a /messages route and a DMs tab), so declaring false would be inaccurate. Flagged rather than changed quietly, because an age-rating answer is a declaration to Apple and is the user's to make. ageAssurance must be present or the PATCH 409s; ageRatingOverride V1 must NOT be sent alongside V2.

pricing._comment: Free. Apple has no 'free' flag; a schedule pointing at the $0.00 price point for the base territory is how it is expressed.
